# Data Preparation

First, we prepare the working environment.

```{r}
rm(list=ls()) # Clear the environment
# setwd("...")  # Setup the working directory
```

### Installation

Install the jpeg package which we will use for analysis.
```{r}
#install.packages("jpeg")
library(jpeg)
?readJPEG
```

This reads the image of ship which is originally of size around 400 KB. It reads it into an array of size `1200 x 1600 x 3` where the dimensions are `height x width * channel`.
```{r}
ship <- readJPEG("ship.jpg" )
str(ship)
```

![](ship.jpg)
This is a grayscale image where the value of each pixel is a single number that carries the intensity information from 0 (white) to 1 (black) with different shades of gray taking values between 0 and 1. 
```{r}
min(ship)
max(ship)
```
We can also verify that all three channels have the same values (when you have color images these values will be different).
```{r}
max(abs((ship[,,1]-ship[,,2])))
max(abs((ship[,,1]-ship[,,3])))
```

# Singular value decomposition

We will now perform a SVD on this matrix. This creates three objects, namely, `d` consisting of singular values (1200), `u` consisting of left singular vectors (1200 * 1200) and `v` consisting of right singular vectors (1600 * 1200). 
```{r}
?svd
s <- svd(ship[,,1])
str(s)
```
Let us now develop a low rank approximation. As we see the singular values have a few high values and then it quickly drops off.
```{r}
plot(s$d)
```

Let us create a rank one approximation to the matrix
```{r}
s1 <- s$d[1]*s$u[,1]%*%t(s$v[,1])
str(s1)
?writeJPEG
writeJPEG(s1,"s1.jpg")
```
![](s1.jpg)

Let us create a rank ten  approximation to the matrix

```{r}
s10 <- s$u[,1:10]%*%diag(s$d[1:10])%*%t(s$v[,1:10])
str(s10)
writeJPEG(s10,"s10.jpg")
```
![](s10.jpg)

```{r}
s100 <- s$u[,1:100]%*%diag(s$d[1:100])%*%t(s$v[,1:100])
str(s100)
writeJPEG(s100,"s100.jpg")
```
![](s100.jpg)

The first singular value accounts for 84.18%, the first ten singular values accounts for 91.74% and the first hundred singular values accounts for 98.09%.  
```{r}
var <- cumsum(s$d^2)
str(var)
plot(1:1200,var/max(var))
var[1]/max(var)
var[10]/max(var)
var[100]/max(var)
```




# RGB Image


We now repeat the analysis using a RGB image

```{r}
pansy <- readJPEG("pansy.jpg")
str(pansy)
```
![](pansy.jpg)


The figure has a size of 78.8 KB. This is read into an array of size 600 x 465 x 3,
height x width x channel (with each channel representing the RGB intensity.
Note that in this case pansy[,,1] is different than pansy[,,2].

```{r}
max(abs((pansy[,,1]-pansy[,,2])))
```

Let's now perform the Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) on the different channels
```{r}
s1 <- svd(pansy[,,1])
s2 <- svd(pansy[,,2])
s3 <- svd(pansy[,,3])
```

Develop low rank approximation (with rank 50). Initialize the vector for storing the approximation
```{r}
pansy50 <- array(dim=c(600,465,3))
pansy50[,,1] <- s1$u[,1:50]%*%diag(s1$d[1:50])%*%t(s1$v[,1:50])
pansy50[,,2] <- s2$u[,1:50]%*%diag(s2$d[1:50])%*%t(s2$v[,1:50])
pansy50[,,3] <- s3$u[,1:50]%*%diag(s3$d[1:50])%*%t(s3$v[,1:50])
```

Save the image in a jpeg file of size ~40 kb, which has some blurring edges of the flower and leaves.

```{r}
writeJPEG(pansy50,"pansy50.jpg")
```
![](pansy50.jpg)

Let's retry with a higher approximation.

```{r}
pansy350 <- array(dim=c(600,465,3))
pansy350[,,1] <- s1$u[,1:350]%*%diag(s1$d[1:350])%*%t(s1$v[,1:350])
pansy350[,,2] <- s2$u[,1:350]%*%diag(s2$d[1:350])%*%t(s2$v[,1:350])
pansy350[,,3] <- s3$u[,1:350]%*%diag(s3$d[1:350])%*%t(s3$v[,1:350])
writeJPEG(pansy350,"pansy350.jpg") # --> much better!
```
![](pansy350.jpg)
